newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin sees inflation surging in October.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin sees inflation surging in October.

text.p: Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda said on Wednesday he was concerned the Thai consumer price index would rise sharply in October because of a minimum wage increase that would take effect that month, higher oil prices and rising food costs.

Bodi said inflation would be fuelled next month by a scheduled 8.2 percent rise in the Thai daily minimum wage from October 1, sustained high oil prices and more public spending on food in the wake of monsoon flooding in rural Thailand in the past week.

"We need to get economic indicators of the second half of September to see if there are any changes which would likely have sustained impact in October, especially on surging oil prices and flooding. If they are relatively out of control, inflation will definitely accelerate," he said.
The minister said the minimum wage hike may widen the Thai current account deficit as it would raise production cost of Thai exports and undercut their competitiveness.
